[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: API Security — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL enforce API traffic mediation through a centralized gateway capability that provides a consistent enforcement point for authentication, authorization delegation, rate limiting, and schema validation for all externally exposed API endpoints.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to mediate all inbound API traffic through a defined enforcement point
- Token validation and consumer identity verification at the gateway boundary
- Rate limiting, throttling, and request validation at the API entry point
- API inventory and routing governance

**Out of Scope**:
- Fine-grained authorization logic within application business logic (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12)
- Internal service-to-service API calls within a service mesh (see network security domain)
- Network-layer DDoS mitigation (see Network Security domain)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- All externally exposed APIs SHALL be registered and routable only through the designated gateway capability — direct backend exposure SHALL NOT be permitted.
- The gateway SHALL validate the authentication token or credential of every inbound API call before routing to the backend.
- Rate limiting SHALL be applied at the gateway to protect backend services from excessive request volumes regardless of intent.
- API schema validation SHOULD be applied at the gateway to reject malformed requests before they reach application logic.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#traffic-mediation]

#### Traffic Mediation

**Architectural intent**: Establish the API gateway as the single, consistent enforcement point for all externally consumed API traffic.

**Design guidance**:
- The gateway SHALL be the only network path through which external consumers can reach API backends.
- Routing configuration SHALL be maintained through a governed change process; ad-hoc backend exposure bypassing the gateway SHALL NOT be permitted.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#credential-verification]

#### Credential Verification

**Architectural intent**: Ensure every API consumer is identified and authenticated before their request is honored.

**Design guidance**:
- The gateway SHALL verify the signature and validity of bearer tokens on every request.
- Expired, malformed, or unrecognized tokens SHALL be rejected at the gateway with an appropriate error response.
- Token verification SHALL delegate to the enterprise authorization service (GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12) for claims evaluation.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#request-governance]

#### Request Governance

**Architectural intent**: Protect API backends from malformed, excessive, or abusive request patterns.

**Design guidance**:
- Rate limits SHALL be configurable per API consumer identity and per API route.
- Request payload validation against published API schema SHOULD be enforced at the gateway layer.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Consumer Request | Inbound | External / Internal API Consumer | API call received at the gateway |
| Token Validation | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12 | Token claims forwarded for authorization evaluation |
| Backend Route | Outbound | Application Backend Services | Validated, mediated request forwarded to backend |
| API Registry | Bidirectional | API Inventory System | Route registration and consumer registration |
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

The API Gateway Security ABB is a primary enforcement point for the Applications and Workloads pillar of Zero Trust. Every API call is a trust decision; the gateway enforces that no request is honored without verified identity and explicit routing authorization, regardless of network position.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the AC (Access Control) family — specifically mediated access to resources through an authorized pathway — and the SC (System and Communications Protection) family, which addresses boundary protection and the separation of system interfaces.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Gateway architecture must account for latency introduced by mediation; performance requirements must be defined before gateway placement decisions are made.
- High availability of the gateway capability is a critical dependency for all services that rely on it; resilience architecture must be addressed in the Reference Architecture.
- Relationship with GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12 must be clearly delineated; the gateway handles traffic mediation and token verification while APIAZ handles the authorization decision logic.
